items.followUp: Define transpiration and describe the role of stomata in this process.

rubric.why: Defines photosynthesis as the process by which plants make food.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that green plants make food (or glucose) from carbon dioxide and water using light energy; award 1 mark for a partly correct definition.

rubric.why: Identifies light as the energy source for photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that light provides energy for photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Explains that chlorophyll captures light energy.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for explaining that chlorophyll traps or absorbs light energy; award 1 mark if chlorophyll is named but its role is unclear.

modelAnswer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants make glucose from carbon dioxide and water using light energy.
Oxygen is released during this process.
Light provides the energy needed for photosynthesis.
Chlorophyll in the chloroplasts traps light energy for the process.

items.followUp: Describe the location and two functions of the pancreas.

rubric.why: States the liver's relative size among glands.
rubric.description: Identifies the liver as the largest gland.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the liver as the largest gland in the body.

rubric.why: Gives the liver's position in the body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for locating the liver in the upper abdominal cavity, below the diaphragm.

rubric.why: Describes bile's role in fat digestion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the liver produces bile, which helps emulsify fats.

rubric.why: Gives another important function of the liver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the liver stores glucose as glycogen or detoxifies harmful substances.

modelAnswer: The liver is the largest gland in the human body.
It lies in the upper abdominal cavity, below the diaphragm.
It produces bile, which helps emulsify fats during digestion.
It stores excess glucose as glycogen and also detoxifies harmful substances.

items.followUp: What are reproductive organs? Give two examples.

rubric.why: Identifies the main vegetative organs of a plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming roots, stems and leaves as the vegetative organs.

rubric.why: Provides two examples of vegetative organs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving any two correct examples, such as root and stem.

modelAnswer: Vegetative organs are the non-reproductive parts of a plant that perform functions such as absorption, support and food-making.
The vegetative organs are roots, stems and leaves.
Two examples are the root and the stem.

items.followUp: Give two observations that led scientists to investigate the spread of malaria.

rubric.why: Includes the observed association between malaria and mosquitoes or marshy areas.
rubric.description: First observation of A. F. A. King.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for noting that malaria was common in places where mosquitoes were abundant, particularly marshy areas.

rubric.why: Includes an observation relating people's exposure to mosquitoes and malaria.
rubric.description: Second observation of A. F. A. King.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for noting that people sleeping outdoors or without mosquito protection were more likely to get malaria, or that mosquito nets offered protection.

modelAnswer: A. F. A. King observed that malaria was common in marshy places where mosquitoes were abundant.
He also observed that people sleeping outdoors or without mosquito protection were more likely to get malaria.

rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that prions are infectious protein particles and lack nucleic acid.

rubric.why: Identifies the composition or host of viroids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that viroids are small infectious RNA molecules without a protein coat, commonly infecting plants.

modelAnswer: Prions are infectious protein particles and do not contain nucleic acid.
Viroids are small infectious RNA molecules without a protein coat; they mainly infect plants.

items.followUp: State two reasons why organisms are grouped into kingdoms.

rubric.why: Recognizes that classification organizes the diversity of organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that classification arranges organisms into groups and makes their diversity easier to study.
Award 1 mark for stating that classification helps identify organisms, compare similarities and differences, or show relationships among them.

modelAnswer: Classification organizes the great diversity of organisms into groups, making them easier to study.
It helps in identifying organisms and understanding their similarities, differences and relationships.

items.followUp: Define exocytosis and state what happens to a vesicle during this process.

rubric.why: Defines the movement of material into a cell by endocytosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the cell takes in material by the plasma membrane folding inward and forming a vesicle.
Award 1 mark for naming phagocytosis and pinocytosis.

modelAnswer: Endocytosis is the process by which a cell takes in material as its plasma membrane folds inward and forms a vesicle.
Its two types are phagocytosis and pinocytosis.

items.followUp: Define mitosis and name its main stages.

rubric.why: Defines the cell cycle as the sequence of events a cell undergoes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the cell cycle as the sequence of events from a cell's formation to its division.

rubric.why: Names the two main phases of the cell cycle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming interphase and the mitotic phase (M phase).

modelAnswer: The cell cycle is the sequence of events that a cell undergoes from its formation until it divides.
Its two main phases are interphase and the mitotic phase (M phase).
